{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOVRCof88AAAABYqkphg", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4Bn7ElzhCPh6U", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4Bn7El", "number": 3, "title": "Build a from-scratch Rust/Wasm PC-98 emulator with playable browser demo (v0.1)", "body": "## Problem

`pc98-rust` currently has collaboration documentation but no emulator implementation. The first deliverable must **already run in a web browser**, execute actual NEC PC-98 machine code, accept PC-98 software/disk images, and provide a legally redistributable working demo. A CPU-only skeleton, static mock screen, or UI that does not execute guest code is not sufficient.

Implement the hardware emulation **from scratch in Rust**: do not embed, translate, fork, or depend on an existing x86/PC-98 emulation core, CPU emulator, GDC, FM chip emulator, or other emulation library. Ordinary build, Wasm bindings, web UI, audio, testing, and tooling libraries are allowed.

## Expected outcome

A self-contained, locally servable browser app with a Rust-compiled WebAssembly emulation core. Opening the app and selecting the included demo starts a real, interactive PC-98 program. Users can also load their own supported PC-98 floppy images and operate the guest with a PC-98 keyboard layout. It renders real guest text/graphics and produces available guest audio (at least the built-in beeper). A reproducible native/headless test path exercises the same core, and PR-time automated browser tests prove the shipped artifact runs **before merge**.

### Machine profile and compatibility scope

Start with **one documented PC-9801VM-family profile**, rather than claiming to support every PC-9801/PC-9821 model. NEC lists the PC-9801VM4 as V30 at selectable 8/10 MHz, up to 640 KiB user RAM, 12 KiB text VRAM, 192 KiB graphics VRAM, 640×400 graphics, 8 simultaneous colors from a 4096-color palette, and two floppy drives. See [NEC specification](https://support.nec-lavie.jp/support/product/data/spec/cpu/b183-1.html) and [PC-98 technical overview](https://pc98.ne.jp/techdet/).

Provide the complete subset of hardware behavior **actually needed for the accepted boot/DOS/demo workflow**, including relevant probing and startup behavior. Do not replace the requested hardware emulator with an INT 21h-only DOS player. Unsupported features/machine generations must be documented rather than silently simulated or claimed as compatible. Later PC-9801VX/RS/9821 16-color, EGC, 80286 protected mode, 256-color PEGC, full HDD/SCSI support, etc. are not automatic v1 requirements unless needed for the chosen acceptance demo.

### Required implementation areas

1. **CPU and execution:** Rust 16-bit real-mode NEC V30/8086-compatible CPU, with 8/16-bit registers, segments, FLAGS, 20-bit segmented memory addressing, instruction prefixes, ModR/M, effective addresses, stack/call/return, arithmetic/logic/flags, shifts/rotates, string and REP operations, interrupts/IRET, IN/OUT, CLI/STI/HLT, and the documented V30-specific behavior exercised by tests/software. A cycle/step budget and deterministic scheduler prevent a guest from blocking the UI.
2. **Bus, RAM, ROM and memory map:** the relevant 1 MiB real-mode address space (including 640 KiB conventional RAM and IVT/BIOS data area), text VRAM approximately `0xA0000–0xA3FFF`, mapped graphics VRAM `0xA8000–0xBFFFF` including planes/pages, remaining model-specific windows, IPL/firmware mapping and reset vectors. Correct memory-mapped vs port-mapped I/O, word/byte access, wrapping and protection. Cite the chosen model's exact map; do not assume IBM PC/AT VGA mappings.
3. **Graphics:** both NEC µPD7220 GDCs (master text and slave graphics) at the command/register/timing level required for boot and demos; text VRAM (character/attribute, cursor, scrolling, glyphs) and bitmap VRAM (planar, palette, page select), GRCG operations as used by target software, and compositing into a 640×400 browser canvas. Provide an appropriately licensed replacement glyph font rather than distributing NEC's font ROM.
4. **Interrupts and basic devices:** cascaded 8259-compatible PIC, PIT/8253-compatible timers, 8237-compatible DMA subset required by FDC, PC-98 keyboard interface (scan codes, key-up/down, modifiers, key-repeat where needed), system/PPI-style ports and clock/status behavior required at startup; IRQ delivery and acknowledgements must work, not be unconditional stubs.
5. **Disk and boot:** PC-98-compatible floppy controller command/status/seek/read/write/IRQ/DMA behavior sufficient for boot and tests; raw 2HD/HDM/TFD/XDF and a documented D88 format reader (other formats such as FDI are optional). Support loading a local image, boot/reset, read/write disk sectors, and exporting modified media or persisting a save state/disk data in browser storage. Validate image sizes/geometry and fail safely on corrupt or unsupported inputs.
6. **Firmware / DOS compatibility:** a **newly written**, redistributable synthetic IPL/BIOS (or equivalent guest-visible boot firmware) providing the actual PC-98 bootstrap and BIOS services required by the demos, including documented INT 18h/1Bh services as needed. Do not bundle NEC BIOS, proprietary MS-DOS, original font ROMs, copyrighted firmware dumps, or other unlicensed material. For DOS applications, use a properly licensed PC-98 DOS (e.g. compatible FreeDOS(98)) as a *guest* OS, not as an emulator library, with license/source obligations met.
7. **Sound:** PC-98 beeper with clocked state exposed to Web Audio and sensible browser autoplay gating. If the accepted gameplay demonstration depends on YM2203/YM2608/OPNA, implement the required sound chip functionality from scratch; otherwise clearly mark optional FM hardware for follow-up.
8. **Browser integration:** build for `wasm32-unknown-unknown` with a small JS/HTML host (Canvas/Canvas2D, keyboard, Web Audio, file picker/drag-drop, run/pause/reset, media insert/eject, error reporting). No server-side emulator execution or required network call after assets load. Limit work per frame; controls remain responsive; do not require a browser extension, physical PC-98, or proprietary files for the included demo.
9. **Testability and documentation:** the Rust core must also run natively/headlessly, expose deterministic stepping, screen/framebuffer/state inspection, and a repeatable mechanism to inject keys and load disks. Document chosen machine profile, covered I/O ports/IRQs/BIOS services, guest media formats, known compatibility gaps, file attribution, and exact local build/test/serve commands. Add CI for the commands actually introduced.

### Demo software and licensing research

Distinguish **firmware ROMs** from PC-98 **floppy disk images / executable programs**; PC-98 games are commonly distributed as the latter. Verify the license **for the particular binaries and assets**, including any bundled boot environment, not merely a repository's top-level badge.

- **Mandatory independently authored boot test:** [HelloWorld-PC98](https://github.com/TakedaHiromasa/HelloWorld-PC98), an MIT-licensed PC-98 bare-metal hello-world/beep program with a prebuilt [`src/hello98.TFD`](https://github.com/TakedaHiromasa/HelloWorld-PC98/blob/master/src/hello98.TFD) and assembly source. Import or reproduce a *license-cleared* copy (including MIT notice) as an automated integration fixture. The original repository also contains tooling and filesystem data: audit any extra copied artifacts separately; do not indiscriminately vendor the entire repository. Boot it through the emulator's PC-98 floppy/BIOS path and verify its actual output; a host-drawn imitation does not count.
- **Mandatory playable demo:** ship a genuinely interactive **PC-98 guest program/game** that runs via the emulated CPU and hardware (not a JavaScript game drawn on top). Prefer an independently authored redistributable existing PC-98 game that fits the VM hardware profile; if no existing candidate has clear distribution rights/profile compatibility, write and license a small original bootable guest game (e.g. keyboard-driven arcade/puzzle demo) and include source, reproducible disk generation, and an end-to-end automated gameplay test. The acceptance criterion is that the browser has a playable guest game out of the box.
- **Real DOS software compatibility target:** validate booting a legally redistributable PC-98 [FreeDOS(98)](https://github.com/lpproj/fdkernel) guest image/installation where compatible, and run a simple PC-98 DOS executable through the guest. [WebNP2's FreeDOS(98) packaging notes](https://github.com/uraraworks/WebNP2/blob/master/README.md#bundled-freedos98-boot-floppy) identify a GPLv2+ 2HD guest boot image and its upstream sources; verify and preserve any required licenses/source distribution. If a particular image is not suitable for the specified VM profile, build/choose a legal compatible guest image and document why.
- **Further candidate, not assumed VM-compatible:** [ADV98](https://github.com/yarufu/pc98) is MIT-licensed and provides a DOS-based ADV engine/sample; its stated 16-color / PC-9821 requirements may exceed the VM profile. Treat it as research/future compatibility material, not mandatory VM proof.
- **Rights caution:** archival freeware is **not** inherently redistributable. For example, [Space Panicco RIGHTS.md](https://github.com/gikonekos/Space-Panicco-Archive/blob/main/RIGHTS.md) quotes an original no-reposting restriction. Do not vendor it without a rights basis. Let users load their own legitimately obtained media.

### Suggested execution sequence (one end-to-end Issue; do not close for partial milestones)

1. Record hardware/firmware/I/O requirements traced to documentation and define reproducible native guest-program fixtures.
2. Implement/test CPU → memory/bus → PIC/PIT/DMA/keyboard → GDC/VRAM/rendering → FDC/boot/synthetic firmware → beeper.
3. Boot the third-party MIT hello-world floppy and capture automated state/framebuffer assertions.
4. Boot the legal PC-98 DOS guest and run a minimal DOS app through the emulated machine; implement missing device/BIOS behavior according to observed tests.
5. Build an actual playable PC-98 guest game/demo; integrate Wasm/browser controls, disk loading, and PR-time browser smoke tests.
6. Finish license audit, documented build/serve/test instructions, CI, and the PR review flow. Make the smallest coherent implementation that satisfies this Issue; avoid speculative additional device models/features.

### Technical references

- [NEC PC-9801VM4 hardware specification](https://support.nec-lavie.jp/support/product/data/spec/cpu/b183-1.html)
- [UNDOCUMENTED 9801/9821 Vol.2, memory/I/O (PIC, DMA, keyboard, GDC/display, PIT, FDD, sound)](https://www.webtech.co.jp/company/doc/undocumented_mem/index.html)
- [PC-98 model/generation technical overview](https://pc98.ne.jp/techdet/)
- [PC-9801VM memory map diagram](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:PC-9801VM_memory_map.svg)
- [D88 disk-image format](https://www.pc98.org/project/doc/d88.html)
- [MAME PC-9801 device/memory mapping](https://github.com/mamedev/mame/blob/master/src/mame/nec/pc9801.cpp) (**reference only, do not incorporate the existing emulator implementation**)
- [Repository development flow](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/development-flow.md) and [AI review/merge guidance](https://github.com/takahirox/pc98-rust/blob/main/docs/review-guidelines.md)

## Context and reproduction

The current `main` contains `README.md`, `AGENTS.md`, collaboration templates, and docs only; it does not contain an application or build commands. Establish actual Rust/Wasm/build/test tooling as part of this application Issue. Baseline reproduction: opening the repository currently cannot launch an emulator or game.

Honor the repository's **Issue → implementation → PR → AI review → revision (if needed) → merge** workflow and English convention. A separate implementer should be able to complete this Issue without asking for a human to perform tests or grant permission for proprietary media. No assignee is required. It is acceptable to use multiple development commits or PRs, but do not claim this Issue is complete or close it on a CPU-only or mock-demo milestone.

## Pre-merge acceptance criteria

- [ ] The emulator CPU, bus, memory, PC-98 display/graphics, required peripherals and guest-visible boot/firmware behavior are implemented in **original Rust** without emulation libraries. A source/dependency inspection and documented feature/port map make this auditable.
- [ ] A documented PC-9801VM-family real-mode profile executes 16-bit guest machine code (not a mock) and passes deterministic native unit/integration tests covering representative CPU flags/instructions, segmentation/wrap, interrupts/PIC/PIT, VRAM/GDC, keyboard, FDC reads/writes, and boot behavior.
- [ ] An independently authored, license-verified **HelloWorld-PC98 floppy** boots through guest FDC + firmware, renders its expected screen output and exercises BEEP; pre-merge automated assertions check guest execution, framebuffer contents, and beeper state.
- [ ] A properly licensed, profile-compatible **PC-98 FreeDOS(98) guest** boots to a usable command environment, executes a minimal DOS executable, and passes reproducible native/headless smoke tests. Record the source/version/checksum/license/source availability of the guest image.
- [ ] The browser can boot and **play** at least one redistributable guest game/demo shipped with the app: a user can affect the game using keyboard inputs, the framebuffer updates because of guest CPU/device execution, and an automated pre-merge playthrough asserts a meaningful state change. An original newly written game is an acceptable fallback only when no suitable existing redistributable game fits this model.
- [ ] The real Rust core builds to WebAssembly; a reproducible local static server opens the browser app, starts the demo without proprietary ROMs/DOS, shows PC-98 output, processes keyboard, and supports loading local floppy images. The included example works offline once served.
- [ ] Automated **pre-merge** browser test(s) (e.g. Playwright) build/serve the actual Wasm artifact, launch the shipped guest demo, assert expected screen/guest state and interaction, and fail reliably on a broken or missing Wasm bundle. Use CI where feasible; include a documented local equivalent.
- [ ] Browser audio initializes after user input and produces guest-driven BEEP; no fabricated host-only sound in place of emulation. Disk/media state can be saved/exported or persisted and is verified with an automated test.
- [ ] The README describes how to build/test/serve, play the bundled guest demo, import personal `.TFD`/`.HDM`/`.D88` media, keyboard mapping, machine compatibility limits, and how demo/guest licenses are satisfied. No proprietary ROM, NEC font, commercial disk, or unclear-redistribution freeware is bundled.
- [ ] Relevant native tests, Wasm build and automated browser tests **actually run and pass before merge**. The PR reports specific commands/results and honestly discloses anything not executed. AI review assesses both missing requirements and unnecessary complexity; do not close this Issue for an incomplete PR.

**Automation / no human gate:** None of these criteria may depend on a post-merge deployment, a published GitHub Pages URL, original hardware, subjective human playtesting, human sign-off, or manual inspection in a browser. Use reproducible tests and machine-readable assertions during the PR. A required action that cannot be automated should be replaced with an automatable equivalent wherever possible; do not silently drop functional requirements.

## Optional validation

Broader compatibility tests with personally supplied, legally obtained period games; comparison against emulator reference behavior (not reuse of code); actual PC-98 hardware checks; FM sound fidelity; other PC-9801/9821 models; 16-color/EGC; additional image formats; GitHub Pages publication and live-site verification. None of these is a merge prerequisite unless a specific accepted demo directly requires it.

## Required post-merge verification

None. All mandatory functional, licensing, and browser checks must be executable on the PR branch before merge; published-site smoke checks may be performed opportunistically later but cannot block AI-driven implementation, review, or merge.
